title: Reflection Debuts First US Rival to DeepSeek With 501B Parameter Model

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock
Nebius Group N.V. Class A Ordinary Shares

summary:
Two former Google DeepMind researchers have launched an agentic artificial intelligence system capable of autonomously handling coding and reasoning tasks. The software, known as Beam, features 501B total parameters and 23B active parameters, and is designed to provide a domestic alternative to lead open-weight systems from China such as DeepSeek and Qwen. Reflection intends to release the full weights of the model later this month, which will allow companies to customize the system using their own private data and compute resources.

The startup has raised $4.6B from Nvidia, Sequoia, and Lightspeed to fund its development and has committed over $7B to compute through 2029. This includes a $1B agreement with Nebius and monthly payments of $150M to SpaceX for the Colossus cluster. While the model aims to match top open systems, industry sources expect it to initially trail the most advanced closed-source frontier systems in the U.S.

selectedTweets.text:
Reflection’s founders on building a DeepSeek of the West

Reflection is soon releasing Beam, its first open-weight AI model, in a bid to become the DeepSeek of the West. Trained from scratch, Beam is designed for coding, reasoning, and AI agents. Reflection's benchmarks put it alongside the strongest open models, with substantially more efficient token economics.

To mark Beam’s debut, I'm joined by Reflection's co-founders: CEO @MishaLaskin, who led reward modeling for Google’s Gemini, and CTO @real_ioannis, who helped create AlphaGo and AlphaZero before leading Gemini’s RLHF effort. Reflection has raised $4.6 billion from investors that include Nvidia, Sequoia, and Lightspeed.

We discuss why Chinese labs pulled ahead in open AI models, how Reflection built Beam, and why the founders think companies and countries will increasingly want to control their own models. I ask how they plan to make money from open-weight AI, whether openness can make these systems safer, and what comes next for Reflection.

Axios also says a new wave of Western open-weight AI models is coming THIS MONTH.

Reflection has already been briefing people in Washington ahead of the launch.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Axios is reporting that Reflection AI is about to release an extremely capable open weight model expected to compete with the top Chinese open weight ones. Reflection have been paying Elon $150 million a month for compute at Colossus since July, on top of a $1 billion compute deal with Nebius, so a strong model is certainly possible.

Sources also told Axios that multiple open source models from other unnamed American labs are also planned to release this month. American OSS Renaissance about to begin? Howard Lutnick has been hoping for something like this for some time, and at one point was reportedly even considering direct government funding to get the ball rolling. The USG wants American open models to compete with Chinese models globally.
